channel.title: The AI Chronicle
channel.description: Daily AI news — India focus and global mix

item.title: Can Orbital Data Centres Solve AI's Soaring Energy Demand? ISRO and Google's Suncatcher Explore Space-Based Solutions
item.description: As AI models consume ever-greater quantities of energy, Google's Project Suncatcher is experimenting with placing data centres in low-earth orbit to harness continuous solar energy, bypassing the land and grid constraints that limit ground-based facilities. ISRO is also reportedly studying the feasibility of space-based data centre technology as part of India's expanding space economy ambitions. The concept, while still experimental, is gaining traction globally as the energy cost of training and running large AI models becomes a critical bottleneck for the industry.

item.title: IT Body NITES Urges India's Labour Ministry to Mandate Work From Home for IT Workers Amid Oil Price Surge
item.description: The Nascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES) has formally urged India's Ministry of Labour and Employment to issue an advisory mandating work-from-home arrangements for IT workers wherever operationally feasible, citing rising fuel costs and the broader economic burden on tech employees commuting to offices. The request comes as oil prices surge amid regional geopolitical tensions, placing renewed pressure on Indian IT workers' disposable income. NITES argues that India's IT sector has already demonstrated its ability to operate effectively remotely and that a formal advisory would provide legal backing for employees to request flexible arrangements.

item.title: HP Launches First Tablet and New AI PC Range in India, Including AMD-Powered EliteBoard G1a
item.description: HP has launched its first tablet in India alongside a new range of AI-enabled PCs, including the HP EliteBoard G1a AI keyboard PC powered by AMD processors delivering up to 50 TOPS of neural processing unit performance. The AI PC range is designed to handle on-device AI tasks such as real-time transcription, image generation, and intelligent search without requiring cloud connectivity. The launch marks HP's entry into India's tablet market and signals the commercial arrival of dedicated AI computing hardware for mainstream Indian consumers and enterprises.

item.title: Delhi HC to Rule on Whether Indian Government Bypassed Tender Process for National Emergency Alert System
item.description: The Delhi High Court is set to rule on whether the Indian government bypassed a competitive tender process when awarding the contract for India's national emergency alert system to state-run CDOT, following a petition filed by Germany-based Utimaco. The case raises fundamental questions about procurement transparency and whether a monopoly arrangement for critical public safety infrastructure is legally defensible. An urgent hearing has been triggered, indicating the court views the matter as time-sensitive given the system's role in national emergency communications.

item.title: UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath Pledges to Make Uttar Pradesh India's Deep Tech Capital
item.description: On National Technology Day, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath committed to transforming UP into India's Deep Tech Capital, citing the state's rapid emergence as a hub for IT parks, manufacturing, and startups. The announcement reflects a concerted state-level push to attract AI and semiconductor investment to India's most populous state, which is already home to the HCL-Foxconn semiconductor joint venture in Jewar. The declaration adds political weight to UP's ambition to rival Bengaluru and Hyderabad as a technology destination.

item.title: Karnataka Plans AI and Deeptech Innovation Centres in Tier-II and Tier-III Cities Beyond Bengaluru
item.description: Karnataka's State Planning and Policy Commission has proposed a roadmap to decentralise the state's technology ecosystem by establishing Karnataka Innovation Orchestration Centers in tier-II and tier-III cities, moving beyond Bengaluru's dominant tech corridor. The plan targets deeptech incubation, applied AI research, and R&D activity in smaller urban centres as part of a strategy to make Karnataka a global model for technology-driven inclusive development. The initiative follows growing concern that Bengaluru's saturation is limiting India's broader tech expansion.

item.title: AI-Enabled Oversight Layer Proposed for Continuous Electoral Roll Monitoring in India
item.description: Following structural weaknesses exposed during the Special Intensive Revision 2.0 process, experts have proposed integrating an AI-enabled oversight layer with the Election Commission's ECINet platform to continuously monitor electoral roll accuracy in real time. The system would detect anomalies, flag discriminatory voter deletion patterns, and strengthen transparency and accountability in India's electoral infrastructure. The proposal represents a significant shift from periodic manual audits to AI-driven continuous surveillance of one of democracy's most critical databases.

item.title: India Pushes for Sovereign Control Over Advanced AI Cybersecurity Systems Amid Anthropic Concerns
item.description: India is actively seeking sovereign control over advanced AI systems used in cybersecurity after concerns emerged regarding Anthropic's Claude Mythos model and its capacity to detect and potentially exploit software vulnerabilities in critical national infrastructure sectors. The push reflects growing government anxiety that dependence on foreign AI models for security functions poses an unacceptable national risk. MeitY is reported to be in direct discussions to secure guaranteed access and oversight terms before such models are deployed in sensitive Indian systems.

item.title: Delhi HC Passes Interim Order Protecting Shark Tank's Aman Gupta's Personality Rights Against Deepfakes
item.description: The Delhi High Court issued an interim order protecting the personality rights of entrepreneur and Shark Tank India judge Aman Gupta after AI-generated deepfake content misrepresenting him was found circulating online. The order goes beyond merely targeting fake AI videos and could establish broader legal precedent for how personality rights are enforced against AI misuse in India. Legal observers note this ruling may reshape platform liability and enforcement obligations for AI-generated impersonation content nationally.

item.title: India's AI Job Market Growing 15–20% Annually, Says Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw
item.description: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw confirmed that AI-related job openings in India's IT sector are growing at 15–20% annually, making it one of the fastest-expanding employment categories in the country. The minister attributed the growth partly to significant data centre investments driven by favourable tax incentives and expanding digital infrastructure including new subsea cable projects. The statement was made in the context of India's broader push to position itself as a global AI hub.

item.title: India's IT Rules and Online Speech: Expert Event Report Flags Censorship and Platform Compliance Risks
item.description: Medianama has published an event report from its April 2026 roundtable on India's amended IT Rules, where legal experts, civil society representatives, and platform compliance teams raised concerns about the scope of content takedown powers, free speech implications, and the burden placed on intermediaries. The report documents specific provisions in the March 2026 IT Rules amendments that experts argue could enable executive overreach in regulating online speech without adequate judicial oversight. The discussion included perspectives on how platform compliance frameworks may structurally disadvantage smaller Indian publishers and independent journalists.

item.title: Kerala Citizen Builds Crowd-Sourced Website to Track Power Cuts Across All 14 Districts in Real Time
item.description: Alkesh Das, frustrated by frequent and unannounced power cuts, built a crowd-sourced platform that now allows thousands of Kerala residents to report and track electricity outages across all 14 districts of the state in real time. The tool aggregates citizen-submitted data to create a live map of power disruptions, giving households and small businesses advance notice and helping them plan around blackouts. The platform has grown organically with no institutional backing, driven entirely by community participation.

item.title: India's First Orbital Data Centre Satellite: What the Pixxel-Sarvam AI Partnership Actually Involves
item.description: The Hindu has published an explainer on India's first orbital data centre satellite, a planned mission by Pixxel and Sarvam AI that would place AI compute infrastructure in low-earth orbit, enabling satellite-based AI data processing far from terrestrial energy and cooling constraints. The piece outlines what an orbital data centre is, why global firms are racing to develop the concept, and what the specific Pixxel-Sarvam collaboration entails for India's space and AI ambitions. The mission is scheduled for 2026 and represents a convergence of India's private space sector and its generative AI ecosystem.

item.title: Paytm Rules Out NBFC Licence Plans, Stays Silent on Wallet Revival as It Pivots to Agentic AI Strategy
item.description: Paytm has publicly ruled out applying for a Non-Banking Financial Company licence, distancing itself from rivals pushing deeper into lending, while remaining silent on whether it will seek revival of its payments wallet licence following the RBI's crackdown on its payments bank arm. The company's Q4 FY26 earnings call instead indicated a strategic pivot toward agentic AI capabilities and wealthtech services as its primary growth engines. This positions Paytm as an AI-first fintech platform rather than a traditional financial services provider.

item.title: Kissht Fintech Makes Strong Stock Market Debut With Shares Up 22% After Rs 926 Crore IPO
item.description: Digital lending platform Kissht made a strong debut on Indian stock markets with its shares rising 22% on listing day, following a Rs 926 crore IPO comprising both a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale. The listing reflects continued investor confidence in India's digital lending sector despite regulatory scrutiny around consumer credit practices. Kissht primarily targets underserved borrowers seeking small-ticket consumer loans, operating in a segment that remains largely untouched by traditional banks.

item.title: Swiggy and Magicpin Report Improving Delivery Times as Gig Workers Return to Indian Cities After Elections
item.description: Food delivery platforms Swiggy and Magicpin have reported improving delivery times as gig workers return to urban centres following state elections and the peak harvest season, both of which had drawn large numbers of delivery partners back to rural areas. The temporary workforce contraction had stretched delivery windows and reduced platform reliability for urban consumers. Both companies expect full normalisation of delivery operations within days as rider availability recovers.

item.title: Meesho Posts Rs 166 Crore Loss in Q4 FY26 Despite 47% Revenue Jump and 264 Million Active Users
item.description: Meesho reported a 47% year-on-year revenue increase in Q4 FY26, supported by 264 million annual transacting users and a 45% rise in order volumes, even as average order values dipped slightly. Despite strong top-line growth, the company remained loss-making with a Rs 166 crore deficit for the quarter, reflecting continued investment in logistics and platform expansion. Meesho's scale makes it one of the largest e-commerce platforms serving price-sensitive consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 Indian cities.

item.title: Anthropic's Mythos AI Model Is a Double-Edged Sword — It Finds and Can Exploit Cyber Vulnerabilities
item.description: The Hindu's analysis of Anthropic's Mythos AI model highlights its dual-use nature: it can identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities that human analysts miss, but it can equally generate working exploits — potentially placing advanced cyberattack capabilities in the hands of non-experts. This capability is particularly alarming for India's critical infrastructure sectors, including banking, telecommunications, and government systems, which have historically operated with slower patch cycles. The piece contextualises Mythos within India's ongoing negotiations with Anthropic and CERT-In's preparedness assessments.

item.title: US Official Warns India to Avoid AI Dependencies on Adversarial Nations as US-India Tech Partnership Deepens
item.description: A senior US official has urged India to avoid building strategic dependencies on adversarial nations in AI development, framing openness and trusted partnerships as essential to unlocking AI's economic potential. The statement signals a deepening US-India alignment on AI supply chain security, with both governments emphasising regional access to world-class technology. The remarks come amid India's rapid GPU capacity expansion and growing scrutiny of Chinese AI hardware and software inputs.

item.title: IndiaAI Mission Startups Hit by Paperwork Delays — Funding and IP Concerns Stall Momentum
item.description: Startups selected under India's IndiaAI Mission are facing delays in formal agreement signings, with pending MoUs holding up non-compute support and raising intellectual property ownership concerns among founders. While compute access has been provisioned, operational hurdles are pushing timelines and dampening the program's early momentum. The government is reportedly exploring advance payment mechanisms to address cash-flow pressures on participating startups.

item.title: Fi Money Shuts Consumer Banking, Pivots to AI and Enterprise Tech After Co-Founder Gwalani Exits
item.description: Fi Money co-founder Sumit Gwalani has stepped down after six years, following the March 2026 shutdown of the neobank's consumer banking service and a broader strategic pivot toward AI and enterprise technology. The departure underscores the mounting pressures facing India's neobanking sector, where regulatory constraints on banking partnerships have made pure-play consumer neobanking increasingly difficult to sustain. The company's shift toward enterprise AI signals a growing trend of Indian fintech startups repositioning away from consumer finance toward B2B AI services.

item.title: OpenAI Adds Trusted Contact Safety Feature to ChatGPT to Flag Self-Harm Conversations in Real Time
item.description: OpenAI has rolled out a Trusted Contact feature in ChatGPT that allows users to designate a contact person who will be notified by email or SMS if the AI detects self-harm conversations, with the contact informed of their role at the point of being added. The feature is directly relevant to India where ChatGPT usage is growing rapidly and mental health support infrastructure remains uneven. It represents one of the most concrete AI safety guardrails yet built into a major consumer AI platform for vulnerable users.

item.title: Adobe Opens New Noida Office With AI Innovation Focus as India Deepens Its Role in Global R&D
item.description: Adobe has expanded its India footprint with a new office in Noida, explicitly positioned as a centre for advancing AI-driven innovation and marking what the company calls an important milestone in driving global product development from India. The opening reflects a broader trend of multinational technology firms deepening their India R&D and AI engineering presence as Indian talent pools grow. Adobe has significant India operations and the new facility is expected to support work on AI-powered creative and document tools.

item.title: IIT Madras Opens First US Centre in Silicon Valley to Bridge Indian Deeptech Research and Global Markets
item.description: IIT Madras has established its first overseas centre in Silicon Valley, aimed at serving as a launchpad for Indian deeptech startups through research commercialisation and connections with the US tech ecosystem. The centre is intended to help Indian founders and researchers translate laboratory innovations into globally competitive products. This move comes as India accelerates efforts to build a deeptech pipeline that can compete internationally in AI, semiconductors, and advanced engineering.

item.title: Zepto Receives SEBI Approval for $1 Billion IPO, Clearing Path to Public Markets
item.description: Quick commerce startup Zepto has received SEBI's observations on its draft red herring prospectus, effectively securing regulatory clearance to proceed with its $1 billion initial public offering. SEBI issued the observations between May 4 and 8 as part of a batch covering six companies, marking a significant milestone for one of India's fastest-growing consumer tech startups. The IPO will be among the largest in India's new-age tech sector and reflects growing investor confidence in quick commerce as a durable business model.

item.title: Swiggy Q4 Revenue Surges 45% to Rs 6,383 Crore as Net Loss Narrows to Rs 800 Crore
item.description: Swiggy reported a 45% year-on-year revenue surge to Rs 6,383 crore in Q4 FY26, with its net loss narrowing significantly to Rs 800 crore as both its food delivery and Instamart quick commerce arms gained traction. The company is targeting a Rs 1 lakh crore net order value for Instamart, indicating aggressive long-term ambitions in the quick commerce segment. CEO Sriharsha Majety cautioned that strategic clarity — not unchecked spending — will determine which platforms survive the current quick commerce boom.

item.title: DesignX Builds Factory OS and Vish.ai to Turn Industrial Data Into Real-Time Decisions for 30+ Enterprises
item.description: Indian startup DesignX has developed Df-OS, a factory operating system, and Vish.ai, an AI decision layer, that convert raw factory data into actionable operational decisions in real time. The platform is already deployed across more than 30 enterprises including Unilever, Hero, and ITC, positioning DesignX as a meaningful player in India's industrial AI space. The solution targets manufacturing efficiency bottlenecks by replacing manual data interpretation with autonomous AI-driven recommendations.

item.title: GoKwik Launches AI-Powered Kwik Ship to Cut Failed E-Commerce Deliveries by 20% Across India
item.description: GoKwik has launched Kwik Ship, an AI-powered logistics platform designed to reduce failed deliveries by up to 20% for Indian e-commerce brands. The system uses AI-powered calls and automated WhatsApp notifications to keep customers informed and provides more accurate delivery time estimates at checkout. The platform directly addresses one of Indian e-commerce's most persistent pain points — high return-to-origin rates caused by failed deliveries.

item.title: Paytm Bets on Agentic AI and Wealthtech as Core Growth Pillars After RBI Payments Bank Shutdown
item.description: In its Q4 FY26 earnings call, Paytm revealed a strategic pivot toward agentic AI and wealthtech services as the primary drivers of its next growth phase, following the RBI-mandated shutdown of its payments bank arm. The company has ruled out applying for an NBFC licence, instead focusing on AI-powered financial tools and investment products for its existing user base. The shift represents a significant repositioning of one of India's largest fintech platforms toward autonomous AI-driven financial services.

item.title: Delhi HC Orders Removal of Deepfake Videos Falsely Showing MP Shashi Tharoor Praising Pakistan
item.description: The Delhi High Court announced it would issue blocking orders against AI-generated deepfake videos falsely depicting Congress MP Shashi Tharoor praising Pakistan, after he filed a petition over the misuse of his identity. The case marks one of the most prominent Indian legal interventions involving political deepfakes during an active security-sensitive period. The ruling signals growing judicial willingness to act swiftly against AI-generated political disinformation in India.

item.title: Proshort AI Sales Coaching Platform Crosses $1M ARR Within a Year of Launch
item.description: Indian AI startup Proshort, founded by Gaurav Mishra, has reached $1 million in annual recurring revenue within its first year by offering real-time AI sales coaching that delivers live insights to sales professionals during customer interactions. The platform targets India's large and growing sales workforce, providing on-the-job AI assistance without requiring formal training programmes. Crossing $1M ARR in year one positions Proshort among the faster-growing B2B AI SaaS companies to emerge from India in 2025–26.

item.title: Ecofy Raises $15M From Mirova to Expand Green Financing Portfolio Across India's Energy Transition
item.description: Indian green fintech startup Ecofy has raised $15 million from Mirova, an affiliate of Natixis Investment Managers, to expand its portfolio of financing products for India's energy transition. The investment marks Mirova's fourth deal in India under its emerging markets climate mandate, underlining growing international confidence in Indian green finance infrastructure. Ecofy targets underserved segments of India's clean energy economy, including rooftop solar and energy-efficient consumer products, with AI-assisted credit underwriting.

item.title: Karnataka Plans Dedicated SpaceTech Testing Facilities and Manufacturing Parks Under DeepTech Decade Vision
item.description: Karnataka has announced plans to expand its role in India's commercial space economy through a DeepTech Decade vision that includes common testing facilities and dedicated manufacturing parks for space startups and MSMEs. The initiative targets reducing the infrastructure barrier that prevents smaller players from accessing space-grade testing environments. Bengaluru, already home to ISRO and dozens of spacetech startups, is positioned as the state's anchor hub for this push.

item.title: India and Japan Sign Quantum Technology and Health Research Cooperation Agreements
item.description: India and Japan have formalised bilateral agreements to collaborate on quantum science and medical device research, aiming to jointly advance science, technology, and innovation partnerships. The deals are intended to foster joint R&D projects and strengthen academic and industrial ties between the two nations. The quantum technology agreement is particularly significant as India races to build domestic capabilities in post-classical computing alongside its AI infrastructure push.

item.title: Zee Sues Nykaa in Delhi HC Over Copyrighted Songs Used in Instagram Reels Ads Without Permission
item.description: Zee Entertainment has filed a lawsuit against beauty e-commerce platform Nykaa in the Delhi High Court, alleging that Nykaa used Zee's copyrighted songs in Instagram Reels advertising campaigns without obtaining licences or paying royalties, and seeking Rs 2 crore in damages. The case could set a landmark precedent for how Indian brands are required to clear music rights before using short-form video content for commercial promotion on social media platforms. Legal experts say the outcome may reshape compliance practices across India's digital advertising industry.

item.title: India's PoS Terminal Shortage Deepens as China Import Disruptions Push Device Prices Up 15–20%
item.description: India's digital payments industry is grappling with a shortage of new point-of-sale terminals caused by disruptions to imports from China and the West Asia conflict, pushing device prices up by 15–20%. Payments companies are being forced to extend the lifecycles of existing terminals and manage their installed base more carefully. The squeeze threatens the expansion of card and UPI acceptance infrastructure at India's retail merchants.

item.title: Hexaware Q1 CY26 Net Profit Rises 7.5% to Rs 352 Crore as European and Banking Segments Drive Growth
item.description: Hexaware Technologies posted a 7.5% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 351.6 crore in Q1 CY26, beating analyst expectations, with revenue growing 12.6% to Rs 3,613 crore. Growth was led by strong performance in Europe and the banking and financial services vertical. The company maintained its full-year revenue growth guidance of 7.6%, suggesting steady demand for its AI-augmented IT services.

item.title: BigEndian Semiconductors Raises $6M Led by IAN Alpha Fund to Commercialise Its First System-on-Chip
item.description: Indian semiconductor startup BigEndian Semiconductors has secured $6 million in funding led by IAN Alpha Fund, with the capital earmarked to commercialise its first system-on-chip product, expand its product engineering team, and deepen partnerships with foundries, IP ecosystems, and OEMs. The raise is notable in the context of India's push to build a domestic semiconductor industry, as BigEndian represents a rare homegrown chip design company reaching commercial readiness. The investment also reflects growing domestic venture confidence in India's semiconductor ambitions following recent government fab approvals.

item.title: Karnataka's ELEVATE NxT Deep-Tech Programme Draws 983 Applications, Nearly 23% From Outside State
item.description: Karnataka's government-backed deep-tech startup programme ELEVATE NxT has received 983 applications, with 213 — nearly 23% — coming from startups outside the state, indicating national appetite for structured deep-tech support. The programme is designed to accelerate startups working on frontier technologies including AI, semiconductors, and advanced engineering. The strong cross-state response signals that India's deep-tech startup ecosystem is maturing beyond Bengaluru's traditional boundaries.

item.title: Freo Acquires Credit Marketplace IndiaLends to Serve Over 50 Million Users via Combined Platform
item.description: Bengaluru-based digital banking platform Freo has acquired IndiaLends, a credit marketplace, in a move that will give the combined entity access to more than 50 million users. IndiaLends will continue to operate as a separate brand while leveraging Freo's digital banking infrastructure. The acquisition consolidates two platforms targeting overlapping segments of India's underserved credit market.

item.title: Swiggy Q4 Revenue Surges 45% to Rs 6,383 Crore as Net Loss Narrows to Rs 800 Crore

item.title: Delhi HC Bars Tech YouTubers TechWiser and TechBar From Criticising AI+ Smartphones Without Hearing Them
item.description: The Delhi High Court has issued an ex-parte order restraining technology content creators TechWiser and TechBar from making disparaging statements about a brand called AI+ Smartphones, without giving the creators an opportunity to be heard before the order was passed. The case raises urgent questions about the use of interim court orders to silence critical online speech about consumer technology products in India. Legal observers warn that such ex-parte restraints on content creators set a troubling precedent for free expression in digital product journalism.

item.title: Chiratae Ventures Commits $10M to Five Indian Deeptech Startups in Single Deployment
item.description: Chiratae Ventures has committed $10 million across five deeptech startups in India as part of a targeted bet on the country's untapped advanced technology potential. The fund sees deeptech — spanning areas like AI, semiconductors, and frontier science — as an emerging breakout category in India's startup ecosystem. The names of the five startups have not yet been disclosed publicly.

item.title: Paytm Posts First-Ever Annual Profit of Rs 552 Crore in FY26 After Years of Losses
item.description: Digital payments leader Paytm has recorded its first-ever full-year net profit of Rs 552 crore in FY26, swinging from significant losses in prior years. The turnaround was driven by disciplined cost control and a 22% rise in operating revenue to Rs 8,437 crore, with financial services emerging as the primary growth engine. The milestone is significant for India's fintech sector, signalling that large-scale digital payments platforms can achieve sustainable profitability after extended investment phases.
